cause.idle_resume.label: Resumed after a break (cache expired)
cause.idle_resume.fact: After {idle:.0f} min idle, the first call wrote {write:,} tokens of context to the cache again ({wshare:.0%} of this window's usage).
cause.idle_resume.interp: Continuing a large conversation after the cache TTL ({ttl}) writes the whole conversation to the cache again.
cause.idle_resume.advice: Don't resume a large session after more than an hour idle; start a new session.
cause.long_context.label: Long conversation × many calls
cause.long_context.fact: {calls} calls, median context {ctx:,} tokens per call (max {ctx_max:,}); cache reads were {share:.0%} of the session's usage.
cause.long_context.interp: Every call re-read the whole long conversation, so the cost grew with the number of calls.
cause.long_context.advice: Run /compact or continue in a new session, and bundle repetitive work into a script.
cause.cache_miss.label: Cache miss
cause.cache_miss.fact: Cache writes of {write:,} tokens ({share:.0%} of the session's usage), rewritten without an idle gap.
cause.cache_miss.interp: The cache seems to have been invalidated, e.g. by a change of model, settings or context.
cause.cache_miss.advice: Switch models and settings less often while working.
cause.big_input.label: Large input
cause.big_input.fact: Preceding input up to {bytes:,} bytes ({images} images), followed by cache writes of {write:,} tokens.
cause.big_input.interp: A large file, image or attachment entered the context and made every later call heavier.
cause.big_input.advice: Read only the part of a large file you need, and hand over raw text as a file.
cause.parallel.label: Subagents / parallel sessions
cause.parallel.fact: {n} sessions active at once (projects {projects}), {side} sidechain calls, {sdk} headless calls.
cause.parallel.interp: Several sessions used the same limit at the same time.
cause.parallel.advice: Run fewer sessions at once, or run them one after another.
cause.web_research.label: Heavy web research
cause.web_research.fact: {n} web tool calls (WebSearch/WebFetch), {ws} server-side web searches.
cause.web_research.interp: Web results piled up in the context.
cause.web_research.advice: Narrow the research and keep only a summary of the results.
cause.output_burst.label: Output burst
cause.output_burst.fact: {tokens:,} output tokens ({share:.0%} of the session's usage).
cause.output_burst.interp: Long generations took a large share of the cost.
cause.output_burst.advice: Have long results written to a file and limit the output length.
analysis.headline: {label} ({share:.0%} of the window)
analysis.note: Output tokens may be undercounted in the logs
save.idle_resume: Starting a new session would have written about {fresh:,} tokens instead of rewriting {write:,}, and the {later} later calls would each have read that much less (assuming a {fresh_k}k context for a new session).
save.long_context: Running /compact at the start of the window, down to about {t_k}k of context, would have saved each of the {calls} calls about {less:,} tokens of reading (assuming {t_k}k after compact).
save.cache_miss: Had the cache stayed valid, the {write:,} tokens would only have been read, not written again (assuming no model or settings switch mid-task).
save.big_input: Reading only the needed part of the large input (about {tokens:,} tokens) would have kept the rest out of the cache and of later calls (assuming {need}% was needed, 4 bytes ≈ 1 token).
save.parallel: The total work done in parallel is the same, so no saving is claimed. Running it in sequence only softens the spike (how fast the limit is reached).
save.web_research: The logs can't separate how much of the context came from research, so no saving is calculated. Research in a short separate session and carry over only the conclusion to keep the main conversation light.
save.output_burst: The generated output may have been the point, so no saving is calculated. Have long results written to a file.
summary.no_cause: No cause rule matched, so no saving was calculated.

digest.none: No event has a calculated saving.

p.a.sub: Did the progress forecasts on the map (P50, P85) come true? A forecast is a "P50 hit" if the actual total number of calls was at most P50, and a "P85 hit" if at most P85. The targets are about 50% and 85%: higher means the ranges are wide (the safe side), lower means they are narrow. No LLM calls.
p.a.h_week_k: · does it improve as history builds up
p.a.xaxis: x axis = calls at the time of the forecast
p.a.h_docs_k: · documents with a finished checklist only
p.a.note_live: Each forecast the map actually showed is recorded whenever the call count changes, and scored when the agent finishes. Still running: {pending} · unresolved because the session closed before the end: {unresolved} (not counted as misses).
p.a.note_bt: For every finished run, the forecasts at calls 1, 2, 4, 8, … are rebuilt from the runs that finished before it, then scored (the same calculation as moni-token forecast). Time forecasts are not replayed.
p.a.empty_live: No live forecast has been scored yet. They build up here as subagents run and finish (recording starts when this feature is on).
p.a.no_docs: No contract document has a finished checklist yet. When one does, the completion times forecast along the way are scored here.

p.c.e.check_first: press Check with these settings first; it must pass
p.c.g1: Install AWS CLI v2: winget install -e --id Amazon.AWSCLI (or the MSI installer), then open a new terminal.
p.c.g2: AWS console, Billing and Cost Management, Billing preferences: turn on Receive CloudWatch billing alerts. It is free, but it cannot be turned off again.
p.c.g3: Budgets: create one monthly cost budget with no actions and no filters (or reuse one) and note its name. The forecast appears after about 5 weeks of history.
p.c.g4: IAM: create a user with only this policy (replace ACCOUNT_ID and BUDGET_NAME), then create an access key for the CLI.
p.c.g5: In a separate terminal run aws configure --profile {profile} with region us-east-1 and output json. Never paste the keys into Claude or into this page.
p.c.g6: Enter the profile and the budget name here, press Check, then Turn on.
p.c.w1: Only read-only free APIs run: CloudWatch GetMetricStatistics on AWS/Billing EstimatedCharges every {m} min (~{metric} calls a month, inside the always-free 1,000,000 API requests) and Budgets DescribeBudget every {h} h (~{budget} calls a month; budgets without actions are free). STS GetCallerIdentity (free) finds the account ID, which is never stored.
p.c.w2: Cost Explorer (aws ce, $0.01 per request) and GetMetricData (always charged) are refused in code. A monthly cap ({cap} calls) stops every call until next month.
p.c.w3: The free tier is shared with the account's other CloudWatch API use: see Billing, Free Tier.
p.c.w4: Runs only while the agent map task (moni_token map) runs. The status line only reads a local cache file and shows how old its data is.
p.c.org: AWS Organizations: only the management (payer) account sees the billing metric. In a member account the budget alone is used.
p.c.static: This file has no server. To set up or turn on AWS cost, open the live dashboard: {url}
